idea.en: Rotate sixty degrees from the four chamber to face the anterior and inferior walls.

alt.en: Echo Lab render of the Apical two chamber. Rotate sixty degrees with the apex anchored and longest.

caption.en: Echo Lab render of the Apical two chamber. Rotate sixty degrees with the apex anchored and longest.

note.en: Landmarks to confirm: Cavity of left ventricle

steps.en: What you see: The left ventricle and left atrium stand alone with the anterior wall above and the inferior wall below. No right heart should be on screen; the right ventricle creeping in means over rotation.
Landmarks to confirm: Do not accept the view until each of these is on screen.
Common mistakes and how to correct them: Each mistake below comes from the view catalogue with its correction.
Normal values: Left ventricular ejection fraction 52 percent or above in men and 54 percent or above in women is normal, below 30 percent is severely reduced.
Trace endocardium at end diastole and end systole in both the four and two chamber for biplane Simpson ejection fraction.
Report wall motion with the 17 segment model of the left ventricle.

Pitfalls: The anterior wall drops out at depth in large patients, so shift focus there before judging motion. The left atrial appendage may flicker at the edge; do not mistake it for a pulmonary vein.

analogy.en: Landmarks to confirm: Cavity of left ventricle

spot.en: Landmarks to confirm: Cavity of left ventricle
Common mistakes and how to correct them: Aorta creeping into view from too anterior a rotation. Correct it by rotating slightly back toward the four chamber until the aorta clears.
Foreshortened apex hiding true length. Correct it by rechecking length against the four chamber and moving the probe if shorter.
Right ventricle in view meaning rotation has gone too far. Correct it by rotating back clockwise until only left heart fills the screen.

todo.en: How to get it: Place the probe at apex, fifth intercostal space, rotated about sixty degrees from four chamber.
Point the probe marker toward the left, about three o clock.
Anchor on the apex and rotate sixty degrees anticlockwise while watching the right heart leave the screen. Keep the apex at its longest through the turn.
Freeze the image only when every listed landmark is on screen at once.

remember.en: Check the left atrium and its appendage region.

q.en: Which walls does the two chamber show?

why.en: The two chamber faces the anterior wall above and the inferior wall below.

q.en: Why pair the four and two chamber for function?

why.en: Two orthogonal planes traced at end diastole and end systole give biplane volumes.

q.en: Right ventricle appears in the two chamber. What happened?

why.en: Right heart on screen means the turn went too far, so rotate back.

sources: ASE 2019 guideline for the complete transthoracic examination, apical views section.
ASE 2015 chamber quantification guideline, left ventricular function section.
objectives: Rotate sixty degrees from the four chamber to face the anterior and inferior walls.
Pair it with the four chamber for biplane function.
Check the left atrium and its appendage region.
